full.description: This is a micrograph showing a biopsy of oral salivary gland tissue. The image displays a dense lymphocytic infiltrate surrounding and replacing the salivary gland acini. This pattern of chronic inflammation is characteristic of Sjögren's syndrome. The infiltrate primarily consists of mononuclear cells typical of autoimmune exocrinopathy.

random.description: This is a micrograph of a salivary gland tissue sample. The image shows prominent periductal infiltration of lymphocytes and plasma cells. The acinar architecture appears partially preserved amidst the inflammatory infiltrate. These histologic findings are characteristic of chronic sialadenitis, such as seen in Sjögren syndrome.
